articleTitle: Parameters identification of the multispecies Lotka-Volterra model using discrete algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In paper the problem of identifying the parameters of the generalized Lotka-Volterra model is studied. We found conditions under which the discrete algorithm ’’Stripe" proposed by V. A. Yakubovich achieves the identification goals. It is proved that the conditions are not essentially restrictive. The notion of a nonhyperplanar trajectory is introduced. It is proved that for any recurrent nonhyperplanar trajectory, the persistent excitation condition is satisfied.

articleTitle: Neural network-based synchronization control of the two-rotor vibration setup
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This paper considers the application of a learning control algorithm for the two-rotor vibration setup single and multiple synchronization based on speed-gradient method. The primary focus of the paper is to showcase the potential of using neural network control in vibration setups with uncertain parameters. A proposed structure for the learning control system is presented. The neural network was trained using simulation data, considering different values of error in estimating the total energy. The computer simulation results demonstrate the efficiency of a learning control system for vibration setups, which use an artificial neural network to compensate the errors in estimating the current total system energy.

articleTitle: Model of a central pattern generator using a spiking neural network, included different types of neurons
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The performance of various locomotor acts in animals is ensured by the central pattern generators (CPG). The CPG is an efficient system that is capable of independent generation of activity patterns, while the operation of the CPG can be corrected due to sensory feedback. Such properties of CPG are successfully used in robotics. In this paper, we propose a half-central CPG model using Izhikevich neurons. We selected some parameters for CPG neurons, thereby obtaining membrane properties that are close to those of real brain cell membranes that were found in natural neuronal networks. The pacemaker neuron is responsible for generating the rhythm in the network, it is able to generate spikes with a frequency range of 0.3–7.7 Hz, depending on the input signal, which affects the speed of the locomotor cycle. The model is implemented in the Arduino software environment, and in the future, it can be interfaced with a robotic installation that performs rhythmic locomotor patterns.

articleTitle: Consensus time and winning rate based on simulations in two-layer networks with hypocrisy
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: We have developed a new simulation approach for a general concealed voter model (GCVM), called a microscopic version of GCVM. Unlike GCVM, which only uses statistical-physical methods, our approach starts from a real network. A microscopic approach is suitable for any two-layer network (with internal ans external layers) satisfying the definition given in the paper. We have conducted a series of simulations with different network structures and found that a cyclic external structure prolongs consensus time in comparison with a complete external structure. Moreover, a cyclic external structure has a positive impact on a winning rate, and this result is different from the one obtained in the macroscopic version of GCVM. The possible reasons for this difference are discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Classification of brain activity using Synolitic networks
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The purpose of this work is to present and validate a methodology of representing functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data in the form of graphs that effectively convey valuable insights into the interconnectedness of brain region activity for subsequent classification purposes. This paper explores the application of synolitic networks in the analysis of brain activity. We propose a method for constructing a graph, the vertices of which reflect fMRI voxels’ values, and the edges and edge weights reflect the relationships between fMRI voxels. Based on the classification of fMRI data by graph properties, the effectiveness of the method in conveying important information for classification in the construction of graphs was shown.

articleTitle: Simulation of integrated memristive devices and their market prospects
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Simulation of memristive devices has been performed to provide their further integration into nonvolatile memory cells as part of integrated circuits analyzed from the viewpoint of market needs. The model allows us to evaluate the cyclic switching performance of a memristive device, while setting its experimentally determined parameters. Market analysis indicates that this topic is currently receiving significant attention from leading research centers and industry worldwide.

articleTitle: Working Memory Test Efficacy Assessment in Patients with Asthenic Syndrome
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In the current study, we analyzed the results of the cognitive test (Working memory task according to the Sternberg’s paradigm) in patients with asthenic syndrome. To diagnose the severity and type of asthenia, we used the Multidimensional Inventory questionnaire (MFI-20). We propose a new performance metric that considers both the accuracy of the answers and their speed. Our findings demonstrate that individuals with more pronounced asthenic syndrome exhibit slightly higher efficiency in performing tasks related to working memory compared to those with less pronounced asthenia.

articleTitle: Study of low-temperature plasma gas discharge
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The paper presents the results of a low-temperature plasma gas discharge study in order to determine the its combustion mode which provides maximum improvement of the surface layer properties of the machined product.

articleTitle: Using FPGA for developing hybrid system of coupled neuron-like radiophysical oscillators
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: We developed and described with Verilog hardware module for implementation configuring coupling between oscillators. We used it to couple radiophysical oscillators FitzHugh-Nagumo. Possibility and prospects of usage FPGA in hybrid analog-digital systems for flexible configuration of couplings between neuron-like oscillators was shown.

articleTitle: Analysis of connectivity estimates in the pentylenetetrazol rat model of absentee epilepsy using estimating mutual information and phase coherence index
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Detection of epileptic activity is usually based on analysis of brain electromagnetic signals, including Eggs, MEGs, local field potentials and single/multi neuron unit recordings. Pentylenetetrazol is traditionally used to provoke epileptic seizures in healthy animals: rats, mice and guinea pigs. Such pharmacological models of epilepsy allow us to study the work of deep brain structures, including the thalamus and hippocampus, actively involved in the development of pathological activity. The pathological activity in epilepsy is considered to detect in all involved brain areas. However, in some animal models this was not tested properly. Recently we found that in pentylenetetrazol rat model of absentee epilepsy in half of subjects significant part of discharges are expressed only in one hemisphere. So that we decided to assessment of connectivity between brain hemispheres for this epilepsy form. For that we used some methods such as calculating the values of the estimating mutual information and phase coherence index.

articleTitle: Proportion of Similar Neighbours and Optimal Weight of Neighbourhood Contribution in Learning Dynamics of Networked MARL
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Structure of interaction between intelligent agents in networked multi-agent reinforcement learning process is one of important components, affecting learning process and convergence. Interactions of agents, having different objective functions may negatively affect each others learning speed. Network topology was shown to affect learning dynamics. In addition, correlations between nodes were shown to affect optimal proportion of information, assimilated from neighbours, and network correlations were shown to change during learning process. In current paper we explore a correlated network of RL agents interaction, built with respect to a graph density and a proportion of similar agents. The effect of these graph parameters on optimal information volume, used from neighbours, was explored for the environment with three types of users and corresponding three types of messages, sent by RL agents. Learning process maximises users satisfaction. Experiments show 1) the more similar neighbours, the less own information agent needs; 2) increase in density (or in the number of neighbours) may be compensated by their opinion weights, affecting agent learning process.

articleTitle: Assessment of possibilities to improve the efficiency of low-temperature plasma modification of the surface layer of metal products
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Approaches to increasing the efficiency of the low-temperature plasma modification process are considered. It has been established that their effectiveness depends on the quality of the processes accompanying the modification, and increases in conditions where the impact on the processes ensures the stability of its course.

articleTitle: Classification of graph topologies by machine learning methods
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Many objects of the real world, both living and man-made, may be described in the terms of graph theory and represented as graph data. One of the tasks of graph data analysis is to classify graph topologies. This work explored the possibilities of machine learning methods, and in particular graph neural networks (GNNs), to classify graphs with different topologies. The aim was to study the robustness of the classifiers based on graph convolutional networks depending on the samples they were trained on. The authors also compared solutions based on GNNs and non-graph classifiers, which were fed several graph characteristics. The non-graph methods, which included support vector machine, decision trees and linear discriminant analysis, demonstrated results comparable to GNNs with a single convolutional layer on the test sample, but overfitting was clearly visible on the validation sample. GNNs were less sensitive to the changes in the number of vertices. However, GNNs showed a large number of false alarms when classifying regular graphs.

articleTitle: Synchronization in a Network of Neuronlike Oscillators with Memristive Couplings
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: We study synchronization in a network of 10 FitzHugh-Nagumo oscillators connected via memristive couplings. It is shown that the synchronization of oscillators in such network is observed at smaller coupling coefficients than in the case of diffusive coupling of oscillators. Moreover, the synchronization efficiency in the case of memristive couplings depends on the initial values of the system variables.

articleTitle: Oscillatory activity induced by noise in Hodgkin-Huxley-type of model with stable steady state
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The dynamics of the Hodgkin-Huxley –type of model is considered. The Transition from bistable to monostable dynamics is described via a boundary crisis of the bursting attractor. We consider the influence of noise on the dynamics of the Hodgkin-Huxley-type model. It is shown that for a single stable equilibrium, noise can induce oscillatory activity of the spiking-type and the bursting-type.

articleTitle: Analysis of phase synchronization of circuits of autonomic regulation of blood circulation in patients with ovid-19 and other comorbidities
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The work aims to study the degree of phase synchronization of the regulatory mechanisms of circulation in patients with Covid-19 (with and without comorbidities). Arterial hypertension, obesity, diabetes mellitus were considered as comorbidities. A significant decrease in the degree of synchronization has been shown in patients with Covid-19 and other comorbidities.

articleTitle: Two-stage model for epileptic seizures detection on EEG recordings
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to analyze the applicability of a two-stage model based on convolutional neural networks to improve the quality of seizure detection on real EEG data. Wavelet analysis is used for time-frequency analysis. To localize epileptic discharges, the seizure detection task was reduced to the classification task where the prediction process consists of two steps: the first model provides coarse predictions which are refined by the second model trained on the first model’s errors. As a result of using the proposed two-stage model, the F1-score metric was improved by about 2% compared to a single coarse model, and at the same time led to a significant increase in false negative predictions, which shows the tradeoff brought by the considered approach.

articleTitle: Analysis of phase synchronization of circuits of autonomic regulation of blood circulation in patients with ovid-19 and other comorbidities
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The work aims to study the degree of phase synchronization of the regulatory mechanisms of circulation in patients with Covid-19 (with and without comorbidities). Arterial hypertension, obesity, diabetes mellitus were considered as comorbidities. A significant decrease in the degree of synchronization has been shown in patients with Covid-19 and other comorbidities.

articleTitle: A Problem of Nonuniform Deployment for a Discrete-time Multiagent System
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: A discrete-time multiagent system on a line is studied. The case is considered where each agent receives information from some of its neighbors, and there are switching of network topology and communication delays. It is assumed that a segment of the line is given. It is necessary to provide a prescribed nonuniform agent distribution on the segment. A decentralized control protocol is designed. Using the Lyapunov direct method, it is proved that, under this protocol, agents converge to the desired positions for any constant delay and any admissible switching of the network topology.

articleTitle: Development of a self-learning mobile robot control system based on neural networks with long-term plasticity
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The use of spiking neural networks as control systems is an urgent and promising task. Unlike artificial neural networks, spike networks are less demanding on energy resources and have greater computing potential. Also, they are much closer in their structure and functioning to biological neural networks. Therefore, it is very interesting to train a spiking neural network based on the experience obtained with the help of external sensors. Understanding the techniques and methods of training spiking networks will allow them to be used to solve other problems. A spiking neural network with long-term plasticity was trained to control the robot in one-dimensional space. The network independently learned to stop the robot when it receives a signal from a distance sensor that has noticed an obstacle, without touch sensors touching the latter.

articleTitle: Age-related differences in sensorimotor responce during VR-based task performance: time-frequency analysis and functional connectivity
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In the present research, we show the results of time-frequency and functional connectivity analysis of electroencephalography data recorded during VR-based sensorimotor integration experiment. We focus on the differences in visually cued motor reaction processing between two age groups of subjects. Our results provide evidence of compensatory mechanism engaged by elderly adult group of subjects for sensorimotor integration task performance. Besides, young adults demonstrate post-movement beta-rebound, which wasn’t found in older group of subjects.

articleTitle: Explicit Model Predictive Control Design based on Constrained Zonotope Propagation
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Zonotopes have become a widely used tool in control design, demonstrating their effectiveness in various applications ranging from state estimation to explicit model predictive control. However, the traditional use of zonotopes is limited by a set certain geometric shapes that restrict the range of state sets that can be considered. This paper proposes a novel approach to control design using constrained zonotopes that can encode arbitrary polytopes. We present a propagation scheme and an affine approximation of the exact control law for this representation, and discuss issues related to center identification for constrained zonotopes. A fast method for detecting set membership is also proposed based on lifting the constrained zonotopes into a higher dimensional space. The proposed method extends the range of shapes that can be considered in control design and offers a promising alternative to the limitations of regular zonotopes. It has the potential for wide-ranging impact in various areas of control, providing a valuable tool for solving complex control problems.

articleTitle: Attention biomarker based on wave rhythm stability
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of data from a neurophysiological experiment involving various cognitive tasks. The study conducted a statistical analysis of wave rhythm stability and correlated it with average reaction time. The findings confirmed the validity of a previously identified biomarker based on the variance of wavelet energy in EEG signals, demonstrating its effectiveness in reflecting attentional characteristics. This research enhances our understanding of the relationship between wave rhythms and cognitive performance, thereby contributing to the assessment of cognitive load.

articleTitle: Analysis of Complex Cooperative Dynamics Using Joint Singularity Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The paper deals with a generalization of the wavelet transform modulus maxima method for the analysis of the cooperative dynamics of systems including interacting components. The paper presents a generalized wavelet-based multifractal formalism, which is used to quantitatively describe the effect of synchronizing chaos in the dynamics of model systems. Models of coupled Rössler systems and paired nephrons were considered, and changes in the joint singularity spectra during the transition from synchronous to nonsynchronous oscillations in the first model and to the partial synchronization mode in the second model were noted. The results of the study allow us to use the proposed approach to analyze the cooperative dynamics of systems of different nature.

articleTitle: Chimera states in a ring of non-locally connected interneurons
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Chimera states, in which synchronous and asynchronous dynamics are simultaneously observed in a network of identical elements with symmetric connections, are one of the most interesting phenomena in synchronization theory. In our work, we examined the main synchronous states in the ring of Morris-Lecar neurons of the second class of excitability with non-local symmetrical inhibitory connections. Such neurons mimic the activity of interneurons, which are the main type of inhibitory neurons in cortical structures and the hippocampus. The main focus of the study was on chimera states that were detected by the Adaptive Coherence Measure. We assume that these states may possibly be the origin of the interneuronal gamma rhythm in the brain. Also, we developed the ACM approach and showed that for states containing inactive neurons, it is better to use the ACM parameter calculated only for neurons generating spikes.

articleTitle: Altered States of Consciousness are not homogenous during meditation: an fNIRS study
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This study aims to distinguish different stages in functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) unlabeled data recorded during altered state of consciousness. We successfully identified three consistent clusters in each session and observed common patterns among different subjects, specifically a decrease in total hemoglobin levels throughout the experienced condition, which can underlie some common mechanism engaged in the explored process. The obtained results are expected to contribute to the methodology of studying altered states of consciousness, especially on unlabeled fNIRS data.

articleTitle: On synchronization and communication of the robust systems
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this article we study the possibility of achieving synchronization and the communication in the robust systems which are unidirictionally coupled Kuznetsov generators of hyperbolic chaos. Such coupled systems (transmitter and receiver), hyperbolic and therefor robust, demonstrate robust synchronicity states, which can offer high-quality communication even in the presence of distortions in the communication channel. In order to synchronization to take place, it is crucial that frequency distortions do not affect the basic frequency peak n the spectrum.

articleTitle: Reward Planning for Underactuated Robotic Systems: A Study on Pendubot with Parameters Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: There is a burgeoning interest in the field of Reinforcement Learning (RL) across various domains, including robotics. Traditional control approaches for robotic systems, such as semi-definite programming (SDP) or mixed integer programming (MIP), typically rely on the assumption of a known and deterministic model of the environment. In contrast, this study aims to introduce a novel RL method for planning the reward function specifically tailored for underactuated robotic systems with parameter uncertainty. We propose a method with a single RL agent to address the challenge of swing up and balance of a Pendubot system with uncertain parameters. The ultimate objective is to enhance the system’s ability to adapt and perform reliably in the face of varying uncertainties.

articleTitle: Influence of dual frequency auditory signals on FitzHugh-Nagumo neuron network
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The work is devoted to the study of biology-relevant neural networks, which are called spiking neural networks (SNN), and is aimed at classifying two-frequency auditory signals. We consider an ensemble of FitzHugh-Nagumo neurons. Each neuron is connected to a radiophysical circuit tuned to a certain signal frequency. Different clusters of neurons respond to signals with different ratios of frequencies applied to all circuits simultaneously.

articleTitle: Restoration of the hippocampal CA1 area activity by close-loop adaptive stimulation
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The main idea of the project is to integrate an artificial neural network, implemented as an electronic circuit, with microcircuits of the living brain. Depending on the set of input signals, an artificial neural network can produce adaptive generation of electrical signals. We assume that such artificial network, trained using learning algorithms, will be able to simulate brain activity at the cellular-network level. Such neuromorphic system can be used to extend the functions of the brain system or to replace functions lost as a result of pathology or injury.

articleTitle: STRDP: A simple rule of rate dependent STDP
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The temporal and rate codings of information are the two sides of a coin, usually modeled separately. We propose a new learning rule called Spike Timing and Rate Dependent Plasticity (STRDP) that combines both spike-timing dependence like the classical STDP and rate coding capability similar to the rate-dependent Hebbian rule. The STRDP updates the synaptic weights only when postsynaptic spikes occur. The sign (i.e., potentiation or depression) and magnitude of plasticity depend on the time of a presynaptic spike. This learning rule admits a simple online realization, making it convenient for further hardware implementation using, e.g., memristive devices.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Indices Characterizing Skin Conductivity Properties in Stress Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Stress is a detrimental factor to a person's physical and cognitive state. The skin conductance response is one of the non-invasive physiological signals that can be effectively applied to analyze changes in a person's cognitive status during stress. However, despite the large number of studies, there has not yet been developed universal method for quantifying the level of stress, which would be based on the analysis of skin conductivity. The purpose of this study was to compare methods of stress diagnosis using physiological indices derived from the skin conductance response signal. For this purpose, it was conducted a special experiment, including the stages of classical stress tests: the Stroop Color World Test and the Mental Arithmetic Test. The experimental sample consisted of 10 young volunteers in whom the skin conductance response signal (SCR) was recorded. In the course of the work, there were implemented the method of calculation of the oscillation amplitude at successive periods of the SCR signal and the method of spectral characteristics with calculation of the integral power in the band, which turned out to be more sensitive than the implemented method with minor differences. Therefore, the combination of these methods is a promising task in identifying the most effective method for diagnosing stress states.

articleTitle: Concept for epilepsy diagnostics with combined unsupervised outlier detection and supervised data labeling
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In the present work we proposed a concept for epileptic seizure detection based on combination of unsupervised and supervised machine learning algorithms. The first step in the method suggests preliminary EEG marking with unsupervised outlier detection based on extreme value theory. The second step includes more traditional supervised machine learning classifier to separate epileptic seizures from artifacts.

articleTitle: Neuropunk revolution: memristive model orchestrated implants infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this paper, I present the memristive model orchestrated implants infrastructure as the further development of the "neuropunk revolution" approaches. The presented infrastructure uses two tier self-learning infrastructure: (1) memristive minimal spinal cord model; (2) bio-plausible real-time model thalamo-cortical loop-spinal cord implemented as FPGA/ASIC device. The orchestration is based on the bio-compatible models managing bran, spinal cord and muscles stimulation, crating three feedback loops: (1) from pressure on insole and EMG to spinal cord; (2) from spinal cord to brain (thalamo-cortical loop); (3) thalamo-cortical loop.

articleTitle: Epileptic EEG Labeling with Anomaly Detection Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this paper we considered the application of unsupervised machine learning for labeling epileptic human electroencephalogram. We tested the performance of several algorithms specifically designed for anomaly detection.

articleTitle: Memristive Complex Functions for Design of Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This study is devoted to the development of components for a memristive Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network. We propose the electrical circuitry and Simulink simulation of memristive devices, sigmoid, tangent, and forget gates.

articleTitle: How noise impacts on trained echo-state neural network
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this paper we analyse the impact of additive and multiplicative uncorrelated white Gaussian noise on trained echo-state neural network. The network was trained to predict chaotic time series of Mackey-Glass equation. Here we show that mean squared error and dispersion of the output signal produced by trained echo-state network, grows with dispersion of noise sources linearly. Moreover, we show how these two types of noise impact on the statistics of the output signal on the example of dependency of dispersion of the output signal on its mean value.

articleTitle: Hemodynamic response during a short-term memory task
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This study examined hemodynamic response changes during a short-term memory task. Significant differences were identified in the hemodynamic response to high-complexity tasks within the frontal and parietal cortex. Increased oxyhemoglobin levels during later experiment stages suggest adaptation to high-complexity tasks amidst growing fatigue.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation-Based Consensus Algorithm for Decentralized Cooperative Online Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Network systems, that consist of multiple nodes capable of sensing, processing and communicating, estimate some unknown parameters of a dynamic process more accurately due to communication between network nodes. Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition (SCADA) system is a good example of system with different measured parameters. In this paper a decentralized cooperative online estimation with Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation-based (SPSA-based) consensus is considered. The proposed algorithm is a combination of two well-studied parts: Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation and Local Voting Protocol. The numeric example of SPSA-based consensus algorithm applied to SCADA system is presented.

articleTitle: Intelligent system for text-based diagnostics of deviant states of individual
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The article is devoted to the development of the concept of an intelligent system for diagnosing deviant states of individuals based on text analysis using mainly the following text analysis tools: convolutional neural networks, algorithms used by psychiatrists in detecting deviant states of individuals (such as extremism, suicidality, etc.), as well as the theory of information images/representations. Such a system makes it possible to significantly increase the efficiency of identifying such conditions as compared to classical monitoring methods based on content analysis.

articleTitle: Analysis of coupling between low-frequency loops in cardiovascular autonomic system in patients with Covid-19 using cross-recurrent plot
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The work aims to explore the possibility of using cross-recurrence quantification analysis of low-frequency signals of photoplethysmogram and RR-intervals to assess the condition of patients with Covid-19. We used estimates of synchronization of the control contours of the cardiovascular system in patients in the acute phase and a week since the start of treatment. The results obtained were compared with those published earlier and made it possible to choose a more sensitive method of analysis.

articleTitle: Classification of MDD patients with using network measures
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a common and debilitating psychiatric illness that affects millions of people worldwide. Despite advancements in the understanding of its underlying mechanisms, the diagnosis and treatment of MDD remain a significant challenge. In this paper, we present an approach for classification patients with MDD based on their functional network measures. Our results demonstrate that a simple Linear Discriminant Analysis achieves high accuracy (83 %) for two cases: when we use all network’s couplings or when we use only the strongest ones.

articleTitle: Single-Entity Spiking Neuron Models: Survey
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this work, we reviewed different approaches in mathematical modeling of biologically plausible neural systems. Models are characterized and classified based on their common features and special use cases. In addition to spiking models, different types of discrete and continuous analogs are considered to accurately simulate biological processes, including membrane potential dynamics. The models under investigation include neurons and various components encountered in neural systems and affected the dynamics. The selection of specific approaches was driven by their prevalence and innovative perspectives in order to enhance the relevance of the presented information.

articleTitle: Modeling and hardware implementation of vector-matrix multiplier based on 32x8 1T1R memristive crossbar array
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This report presents the results of designing of a vector-matrix multiplier based on memristive devices. Memristive devices are fabricated in the upper layer of metallization, integrating with CMOS digital circuits in a crossbar architecture with 32 bit lines and 8 word lines. The parameters of all electronic components of the system are calculated using SPICE modeling. A prototype of the system has been developed and its operation is shown in the report. Such a crossbar can be a computational core for a neuroprocessor and can be used for hardware implementation of various architectures of neuromorphic systems.

articleTitle: Markers of Acquisition New Word Forms In Explicit and Implicit Contexts with Articulatory Condition: Sources Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: communication using symbols and signs is a crucial specific cognitive ability which distinguishes us among animals. It is difficult to reevaluate the importance of language capacity both in personal and social life of people. Even though the importance of this topic exists, there exists a lot of lack in our knowledge about cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying this ability. Our ability to acquire new semantics of words is one of them. In this EEG study we tried to answer the question how novel word articulation in the word learning task including fast mapping (via context-dependent inference) and explicit encoding (via direct instruction) conditions influences the process of word integration into semantic networks on the sources level. Event related potential data, which exhibited the main response peaks at 180, 550 ms, suggests that learning type doesn't interact with the articulation condition.

articleTitle: Reservoir computing allows recovering hidden network dynamics
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this study, we examined reservoir computing (RC)as a tool for predicting the macroscopic dynamics of a subset of oscillators in a network based on the macroscopic dynamics of other parts of it. As a model network, we utilized a network of 300 Kuramoto oscillators with adaptation. Our results demonstrate that reservoir computing effectively addresses this task. Additionally, a similar reservoir computing model was applied to experimental neurovisualization data and exhibited high accuracy in reconstructing damaged EEG channels compared to classical methods like spatial interpolation.

articleTitle: The influence of perception bias on behavioral characteristics during the interpretation of bistable sensory information
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this paper, an extended experimental paradigm was proposed related to the interpretation of bistable images, Necker cubes. In addition to the classic image of the Necker cube, we shown its mirror projection, which provided left-oriented and right-oriented cubes with a perspective from above and below. We showed a perception bias regarding to the perspective from above, which was confirmed by a lower reaction time, as well as its disappearance with high ambiguity of sensory information.

articleTitle: Regulation of neurogliovascular unit metabolism and vascular tone by arachidonic acid derivatives: Model approach
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Experimental and theoretical studies of brain activity have led to an understanding of the need to consider the interactions between the main components of nervous tissue - neurons, astrocytes, and blood vessels – and to the formation of the concept of the neurogliovascular unit. According to this hypothesis, the interaction of individual elements of the unit is the key force determining the normal functioning of the brain, and disruptions in these interactions lead to irreversible consequences, including the development of various neurodegenerative pathologies. It is known that during astrocytic activity, arachidonic acid is released and its derivatives are synthesized, which directly influence vascular tone, thereby further altering synaptic activity. In this study, we propose a model of the neurogliovascular unit that takes into account astrocytic processes, synaptic activity, and vascular dynamics, considering the synthesis of arachidonic acid and its derivatives. The results of numerical solution of the model suggest that we can control vascular dynamics through the arachidonic acid metabolites profile, including the oxygen-dependent regulation, which directly affect synaptic activity.

articleTitle: Using reservoir computing for dynamics forecast of noise-perturbed FitzHugh-Nagumo system
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: We investigate the capability of reservoir computing to predict the dynamics of excitable FitzHugh-Nagumo model, exposed to Gaussian white noise, and reproduce the phenomenon of coherence resonance in the reservoir. We train the neural network on the dynamics of the system with three noise amplitudes and then test in on different noises. We show that the reservoir computing can exhibit coherence resonance under external stimulus.

articleTitle: Development of Hardware-Software Complex for Detecting a Stress State in Real Time from EEG Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: We have developed an eight-channel device for recording electroencephalogram signals in a wide frequency range including low-frequency oscillations. The signals simultaneously recorded by the developed device and serial recorder have been compared. We have proposed and implemented a method for detecting a stress state in real time. The method is based on the analysis of electroencephalogram signal power spectrum in the range from 0.15 to 0.4 Hz.

articleTitle: Approximate Hindmarsh-Rose model identification: application to EEG data
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The parameters of the Hindmarsh-Rose model are evaluated by measuring the output of the model and estimating the derivatives of the output since direct derivatives measurement leads to poor conditionality of the problem. A "Dirty-Derivative" filter of the third order is used to evaluate them, which gives a smoothed estimate of derivatives. The parameter estimation algorithm is applied to real EEG data and demonstrates convergence of tuning parameters to some values. The obtained parameter estimates are used as features for epileptic seizure classification problem.

articleTitle: Personalized approach in neurocognitive rehabilitation of patients in the acute period of ischemic stroke using virtual reality technologies
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The present study demonstrates the predictive value of neuropsychological markers in evaluating the effectiveness of neurocognitive rehabilitation in patients with damage to the right and left hemispheres in the acute period of ischemic stroke. Early diagnosis of the patient’s cognitive and psycho-emotional functions can be useful in further personalized management of rehabilitation treatment using virtual reality technologies.

articleTitle: Differences in the resting-state functional brain networks of patients with major depressive disorder and bipolar disorder
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this work, we analyzed the functional connectivity between different groups of subjects. The groups included patients with major depressive disorder, and patients with bipolar depression that were obtained during experimental research. The data that had been subjected to preprocessing procedures were employed in order to identify the functional connectivity between the brain regions that displayed significant variations.

articleTitle: Tool condition monitoring using machine learning methods
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The paper presents a method for monitoring the initial and post-operational condition of a cutting tool, based on a qualitative analysis of its surface photographs using a neural network. A method based on the convolutional neural network was developed to analyze the photos. The convolutional neural network is based on an attempt to geometrically combine a wide class of machine learning problems in terms of symmetry and invariance. The results obtained allow us to estimate the fundamental possibility of using a tool for its intended purpose; to determine the conditions for its use if it is recognized as possible; to evaluate the quality of the exploitation process.

articleTitle: Directional couplings between the respiration and parasympathetic control of the heart rate during the cognitive tasks
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The work is devoted to the study of directional couplings between the processes of autonomous control of circulation estimated from the signals of respiration and the sequence of RR intervals during the controlled cognitive tasks. The stressors were called stroop color word test and mental arithmetic test. The experimental sample included 63 healthy men. We calculated the phase coherence coefficient and indices for directional couplings, modeling of phase dynamics. The analysis was carried out in the so-called high-frequency (0.14-0.50 Hz) range associated with the process of parasympathetic control of circulation. As a result, high values of the bidirectional couplings indices between the studied processes were revealed, which changed during the controlled cognitive tasks.

articleTitle: Interaction of the processes of autonomous control of the heart rate during the cognitive tasks
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The work revealed a change in the interaction between the processes of sympathetic and parasympathetic control of the heart rhythm and infra-slow oscillations of brain potentials with a frequency of less than 0.5 Hz during stress-inducing cognitive tasks. Stress test was performed for 63 healthy men. The stress test included Stroop color word test and mental arithmetic tests. Electroencephalogram and the sequences of RR-intervals were analyzed. The signals were filtered in the low frequency range from 0.05 to 0.15 Hz and the high frequency range from 0.15 to 0.40 Hz. The phase coherence coefficient and directional coupling indices based on the method of phase dynamics modeling were calculated.

articleTitle: Development an intelligent method for restoring hippocampal activity after damage
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The main goal of the study is to develop a new method based on artificial intelligence in order to restore activity of damaged hippocampal area. The hippocampus often has impaired functioning due to the neurodegeneration of its individual areas in neurodegenerative diseases, aging, or injuries. In this regard, the restoration of normal activity in the hippocampus based on modem methods of information processing is an important task. We report preliminary results on training a deep neural network with recordings of hippocampal local field potentials. These results showed the possibility of using described approach in the tasks of restoring population neuronal activity.

articleTitle: Multilevel resistive switching in thin oxide films for neuromorphic systems of artificial intillegence: simulation & experimental investigation
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The work shows the results of multilevel resistive switching study in thin oxide films (TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and ZnO), formed by pulse laser deposition. A computer model that allows the simulation of multilevel resistive switching in thin oxide films is developed. The experimental and theoretical dependences of sweep voltage and compliance current effects on multilevel resistive switching in TiO2, HfO2, and ZnO films were plotted. Analysis of the obtained results showed that the maximum number of resistive states, equal to 7, is observed at a sweep voltage of 4 V and a compliance current of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> A. The obtained results can be used in the fabrication of energy-efficient ReRAM elements for neuromorphic systems of artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Pulse duration effect on synaptic plasticity of ZrO2(Y)-based memristive device
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This report presents a method for controlling the synaptic plasticity of memristive devices based on changing not only the amplitude of control pulses, but also their duration. The object of study in this work is a ZrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(Y)-based memristive device due to the demonstrated high stability of its resistive switching parameters. It is established that, when a sequence of pulses with varying duration and positive amplitude ≤ +1.0 V is applied, there is no change in the resistive state. At the amplitudes > +1.0 V, the resistance of memristive device increased significantly with increasing pulse duration. It is shown that the dependencies of the average current on the pulse duration can be satisfactorily approximated by an exponential decay function. The proposed protocol is demonstrated to be more efficient for controlling the synaptic plasticity of memristive devices.

articleTitle: Features of the resting-state functional network in patients with major depressive disorder: mutual information analysis in fMRI data
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this work, we conducted the analysis of the functional magnetic resonance imaging data in healthy subjects and patients with major depressive disorder that were obtained during experimental research when subjects were resting. The signals that have undergone preprocessing and filtration were used to find the functional connectivity between the brain regions. Results demonstrate significant changes between functional connections based on the mutual information measure. We obtained five significantly changed connections, four of which increased more in cotrol group over patients.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Events Recognition in Calcium Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Calcium signaling is essential mechanism in memory formation and learning. The slightest disturbance of calcium metabolism in the neural cells of the system leads to memory impairment and cognitive decline. In this study, we proposed an algorithm for detecting calcium events in imaging data and applied it to in vitro data from the HIF-1 study.

articleTitle: Possibilities and features of the elementary cognitive and educational functions development
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The paper discusses research aimed at studying the possibilities of the development of elementary cognitive functions. Various methods of development and their impact on children in the learning process are considered.

articleTitle: Detecting fatigue indicators from electroencephalogram data during prolonged cognitive load
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Identifying and monitoring indicators of fatigue during various cognitive exercises is an important task in the field of cognitive load research and human performance optimization. Fatigue monitoring allows to evaluate the degree of subject’s involvement in the process and improve the efficiency of task performance. The current study compared two methods to determine potential indicators of fatigue during different cognitive tasks in 21 subjects. The first method is based on an algorithm for calculating the relative power of electroencephalographic activity (α + θ)/β. The second method is based on electrooculogram extraction and analysis of various blink characteristics. In particular, the positive amplitude-velocity ratio (pAVR) was evaluated. The applicability of the algorithms to fatigue detection in cognitive tasks was compared.

articleTitle: Development of a new FitzHugh–Nagumo type simplified electronic neuron
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This study aims to develop a new electronic realization of FitzHugh–Nagumo neuron. We based our work on a previously constructed circuit and modified it to reduce the number of elements. All modeling was done using ngSPICE circuit simulator. For the new developed circuit current-voltage characteristics were constructed, then dependence of signal amplitude on resistance of potentiometer was measured. By this way, we found that oscillations were bom as a result of Andronov–Hopf bifurcation like in the FitzHugh–Nagumo neuron. The different approximations of nonlinear function were considered and the dependence of the output signal on the number n of diodes in the circuit was studied. It was found that signal becomes more pulse-like with increase of n: the fewer diodes used, the smoother the peak was, up to the plateau-like segment for n = 1. At the same time, the dependence of the oscillation frequency on n is weak: in general, the period decreases slightly with increasing n. As a result, we developed a new simplified silicon neuron of FitzHugh–Nagumo type simple for hardware realization and modification.

articleTitle: Development of a statistical methodology for assessing the functional outcome and effectiveness of restorative treatment of patients with cognitive impairment in the acute period of ischemic stroke
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The work demonstrates the feasibility of developing and applying a mathematical model based on correlation analysis using a system of informative clinical and paraclinical indicators to assess the prognosis regarding the effectiveness of rehabilitation and the functional outcome of a patient in the acute period of ischemic stroke.

articleTitle: Influence of TMS-Coil Position on the Lateralization of Phosphenes Elicited by Magnetic Stimulation of the Visual Cortex
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This study examines the dependence of phosphene position in the visual field on the site of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS). We found a strong negative correlation between the x-coordinate of the phosphene position in the visual area and horizontal position of the stimulation coil. It demonstrates the presence of a stable relationship between phosphene lateralization and TMS coil displacement in the horizontal plane. Obtained results can be valuable for the development of brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) with direct feedback including virtual reality applications.

articleTitle: Study of cortical characteristics in operators of BCI with tactile feedback
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: A Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) is a technology that enables the exchange of information between the brain and external devices by processing electrical signals from the cerebral hemispheres. This technology can be applied in the development of neurotrainers for individuals who have had a stroke. In this work, we examined the classification accuracy of motor imagery-based Brain-Computer Interfaces with tactile feedback and assessed corticospinal excitability. The study has shown that the EEG signal classification accuracy results were compared between two BCI variants: one without feedback and one with tactile feedback. The average results across all participants showed no statistically significant difference, with accuracy rates of 63.04% for BCI without feedback and 65.58% for BCI with tactile feedback. We found that when participants engaged in imagined movements, there was a statistically significant increase in MEP amplitude compared to a "rest" state, regardless of their prior training. This suggests an increase in corticospinal excitability during imagined movements.

articleTitle: Astrocyte Activation Modulates Neural Network Activity of Primary Hippocampal Cell Cultures in Vitro
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The role of astrocytes in modulating neural network activity is a topic of great interest that is still not fully understood. In this study, optogenetic methods were employed to selectively activate astrocytes in primary hippocampal cell cultures, aiming to investigate the impact of astrocytes on bioelectric neural network activity. To achieve astrocyte activation, the AAV—GFAP—ChR2—eYFP—WPRE viral vector was utilized to express the ionotropic channel rhodopsin—2 (ChR2) specifically in astrocytes. By employing multielectrode arrays, the study demonstrated that light stimulation of astrocytic ChR2 led to an increase in the number of spikes within a burst and the occurrence of larger network bursts. These changes in network activity returned to their original levels within two hours after stimulation. Additionally, a slight reduction in spontaneous bioelectrical activity in the cultures was observed 24 hours post—stimulation.

articleTitle: Identification of Group of FitzHugh-Nagumo Neuron Models Based on the Speed-Gradient and Filtering
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The paper is devoted to the identification problem of the group of neurons model composed from the FitzHugh-Nagumo single neuron models. The model of N uncoupled neurons and the model of the neural network with the simplest connections are considered. The problem is solved under the realistic condition: only one variable of the FitzHugh-Nagumo model, namely the membrane potential, is measured; however, we assume that this variable’s measurement is imprecise.

articleTitle: Mathematical model of the photoplethysmogram and electrocardiogram signals with a priory known pattern of the phase synchronization
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: We developed a mathematical model of the coupled photoplethysmogram and electrocardiogram signals, which can be used to test nonlinear dynamics and machine learning algorithms for detection of the phase synchronization between the low-frequency (0.04-0.15 Hz) components of the real-world signals. In the model the instantaneous phases of the low-frequency components and their difference are known a priory, and, therefore, can be referenced during testing. The phase difference quantitatively reproduces the spectral characteristics of the phase noise present in the experimental signals and other statistical properties, namely the distributions for the durations of the horizontal and sloping sections of the phase difference, which correspond to the intervals of phase synchronization and desynchronization between the signals. The model qualitatively simulates the shape of the experimental electrocardiogram and photoplethysmogram signals, and quantitatively simulates their power spectra.

articleTitle: Higher-order interactions in functional brain networks in major depressive disorder
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Neuroscience explores the anatomy, function and development of the central and peripheral nervous system. Neuroscientists lately study functional brain networks to understand mental disorders like depression. Analysis of these networks can aid in diagnosing depression. Q-analysis, a higher-order interaction approach, may be more effective in identifying brain regions relevant to depression, compared to the standard paired approach. This study examined functional brain networks, by using higher-order interaction approach with Q-analysis method, in depressed patients and healthy subjects using fMRI data. Results indicated fewer and weaker higher-order interactions in depressed patients compared to controls. Modularity and clustering were also reduce in depression. These findings highlight the importance of studying higher-order interactions in functional brain networks for diagnosing and understanding depression.

articleTitle: Neurophysiological mechanisms of visual sensory information processing in stimuli with high and low ambiguity
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this paper we studied neurophysiological mechanisms of brain information processing and following interpretation of visual stimuli with high and low levels of ambiguity. For visual stimuli we used images of the Necker cube which can be perceived in one of two ways — left- or right-oriented, and this interpretation is highly affected by the ambiguity of the stimulus. We demonstrated that visual sensory information processing of unambiguous and ambiguous visual stimuli follows different scenarios. For unambiguous visual information processing is accompanied by an increase of EEG spectral power in the delta frequency range in the occipital brain region. With increasing ambiguity of visual information, higher spectral power is observed in the delta and theta ranges in the frontal brain region.

articleTitle: Memristive structures based on TiO2 nanodots: simulation, formation and resistive switching
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This research investigates the distribution of electric field strength and conductive filaments in TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-nanostructures formed via the local anodic oxidation method. The study considers models that account for the generation/recombination processes of oxygen vacancies and their migration under the influence of an electric field in defect-free point oxide structures. The bottom electrode consists of a titanium film, and the shape of the oxide nanostructure corresponds to the local anodic oxidation technology. The microscope probe with a 50 nm tip radius serves as the top electrode. The study revealed the features of the formation of conductive filaments in nanoscale memristive titanium oxide nanostructures, which are important to take into account in field measurements.

articleTitle: Performing decision-making tasks through dynamics of recurrent neural networks trained with reinforcement learning
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this work, recurrent neural networks are considered as functional models that perform target tasks inspired by cognitive neuroscience experiments. These networks are trained with reinforcement learning methods, after that structure and dynamics mechanisms underlying their behaviors are studied. We use two versions—with and without a context signal—of the cognitive perceptual decision-making task. Population and single-neuron dynamics are studied resulting in stimulus processing as well as successful completing the target tasks. Functionally specialized neurons as well as cluster structure of the trained networks are found and investigated. Similarities and differences between the model neural networks and biological prototypes are discussed.

articleTitle: Switching dynamics of memristive device under periodic pulse stimulation
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: The study of switching dynamics of memristive devices is a topical direction both in fundamental and applied investigation of memristive technologies. The main problem in this field is a stochastic nature of switching between resistive states of memristive device. This feature leads to the large variance of resistive states during switching and difficulties in setting specific intermediate states of memristive device. We propose the novel method of setting intermediate states of memristive device by controlling parameters of external pulse stimulation. We have demonstrated experimentally the possibility of switching and holding the resistive states of memristive device by pulse-width modulation (PWM).

articleTitle: Competitive Influence in a Social Network with Stubborn Agents: A Case of Constant Control
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This paper studies an opinion dynamics game with active and passive agents. Using a well-established model of opinion dynamics, we formulate the problem as a linear-quadratic game with competing agents. We study the Nash equilibrium as a solution concept under the assumption that active agents choose the same actions throughout the game in order to minimize their cost functionals.

articleTitle: Change in the directional coupling between the heart beat and respiration during the Stroop test and mental arithmetic test
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Purpose of the work is to study the influence of cognitive tasks on the interaction between the processes of autonomic regulation of the cardiovascular system and respiration. The low-frequency components (0.05-0.15 Hz) of the time intervals between heart contractions and photoplethysmogram signals were analyzed using a sensitive method for detecting directional coupling based on modeling the dynamics of instantaneous phases of oscillations. It was shown that the coupling coefficients in the frequency band of 0.05-0.15 Hz (associated mainly with the sympathetic regulation of blood circulation) decrease during the execution of the Stroop test and the mental arithmetic test. It has also been shown that the interaction of airflow signals and interbeat interval is reduced during the execution of a mental arithmetic test The results obtained allow us to better understand the features of the interaction of the elements of the autonomic regulation of blood circulation.

articleTitle: Information Flows in Continuous-Time Stochastic System as Dynamical Causal Effects
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: Methods for estimation of directional (causal) couplings in complex systems from time series constitute a wide field of research with applications in different disciplines including physics, climate science, neuroscience, etc. Among multiple quantisers of causality, "information flows" (IFs) are defined in diverse ways, transfer entropy (TE) and Liang – Kleeman information flow (LKIF) are the most popular IFs with many interesting applications. So, their numerical relationships are of importance, but still far from being fully understood. The recently proposed framework of dynamical causal effects provides a unifying formalism for causality quantifiers which is a convenient tool to study such relationships. Within that framework, the present work reveals numerical relationships between the TE and the LKIF in an exemplary stochastic system of coupled noise-driven overdamped oscillators. Those relationships appear to be quite diverse, depending essentially on parameters of the system. The obtained results allow a better justified interpretation of the numerical values of both IFs that should make their practical applications more fruitful.

articleTitle: Rotating Wave Dynamics in Rings of Coupled Oscillators: Insights into Working Memory Models
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This paper explores rotating waves, a captivating synchronization phenomenon observed in interconnected oscillators. These waves emerge from phase differences between neighboring oscillators, giving rise to stable periodic, quasiperiodic, or chaotic orbits. Rotating waves are observed in diverse non-linear systems like electrical circuits, neural models, and various oscillators. The study employs techniques such as time series and phase-space analyses, bifurcation diagrams, power spectra, and basins of attraction to unveil the intricate dynamics. These methods reveal the route from stable equilibria to hyperchaos through a series of bifurcations with increasing coupling strength, including Andronov-Hopf, torus, and crisis bifurcations. Notably, the research identifies instances of multiple coexisting rotating waves under the same parameters. Special attention is given to neural oscillators due to their significance in brain neural rings associated with working memory. The study of rotating waves finds broad relevance in fields like lasers, chemical reactions, cardiorespiratory systems, and particularly neural networks and brain function.

articleTitle: Predicting of functional results and rehabilitation efficiency of patients with cognitive impairments in the Ischemic Stroke Acute Period based on IQCODE parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In the present study, the possibilities of using IQCODE as a prognostic marker of the functional outcome of patients in the acute period of ischemic stroke are observed. The results demonstrate that pre-stroke cognitive impairment reduces daily activities, independence and the degree of recovery of motor and cognitive functions of the patient

articleTitle: Optimal physical activity index based on digital heart rate data
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In order to improve health, longevity and prevention of non-infectious diseases, the issue of personalization of physical activity is becoming increasingly relevant. The article deals with the index of recreational physical activity, which is characterized by: personification, dynamic change in time, normalization (from 0 to 100) and the presence of three zones to assess the weekly physical activity of a person. The data used to calculate the index is based on daily heart rate (pulse) values. The Optimal Physical Activity Index is an extension of the Optimal Physical Activity Management methodology.

articleTitle: C.R.A.B.: The Paradigm to Study Motor-Related Cortical Potentials in Children
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In the current paper, we propose a novel paradigm to study motor-related cortical potentials: C.R.A.B. (Contrasting Routines Affecting Bereitschaftspotential). The paradigm is gamified in order to be easily transferred to the clinical children population in future studies. The typical "Libet-type" clock is replaced for this type of research by the gradual movement of the crab characters on the screen. Different modes of hide-and-seek game between the characters allowed to induce different decision-making scenarios during (and before) the movement initiation process. In particular, we used conditions with different availability of the external stimuli used as hints concerning the current position of the hiding crab, and a control condition with no hinting stimuli. As a result, we showed that readiness potential waveforms are decreased in the condition, where participants could choose the right movement immediately after trial onset based on visual hints in comparison to conditions with non-reliable hint and no-hint conditions. We suggest that our results favor the interpretation of the readiness potential as a counterpart of the contingent negative variation, reflecting rather an anticipation of a particular movement-related stimulus than the movement initiation (or movement-related intention) per se.

articleTitle: A new method for studying the structure of chemo-mechanical gels used as smart materials
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In the present study, we propose a simpler toolkit for investigating chemo-mechanical gels, which show periodic behaviour and are used in the synthesis of "smart" materials. Research methods for such gels are usually expensive and time-consuming. In contrast, we developed a "one chamber" protocol for freeze drying and obtaining the structure images by scanning electron microscopy in situ without additional transfer between different setups. The proposed new method for the investigation of gels will make it possible to reduce sample preparation time and to study complex morphology without disturbing the structure.

articleTitle: Multiplexing-based control of noise-induced collective dynamics in multilayer networks of bistable oscillators: stochastic resonance and wavefront propagation
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: It is well-known that the presence of noise when occurring oscillatory processes can play both positive and negative role. In the context of bistable dynamical systems, the constructive role of noise is often discussed on examples of stochastic resonance and noise-sustained wavefront propagation observed in a wide spectrum of real-world systems and exhibited by the simplest phenomenological models of bistable oscillators and media. These two effects are widely used in practice, and, for this reason, the issues addressing control of stochastic resonance and wavefront propagation are significant and actual from the point of view of both theoretical and applied science. In the current study, we propose a new approach for controlling stochastic resonance and wavefront propagation in multilayer networks. In particular, we demonstrate that interaction of an one-layer network with another one-layer network through coupling between replica nodes, i.e., multiplexing, allows to control stochastic collective dynamics in multilayer networks associated with stochastic resonance and propagating patterns.

articleTitle: Phase-locked states in a spiking neural network model with a context-dependent connectivity
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a spiking neural network model with Hebbian connectivity that can adjust its activity to input stimuli. The implemented architecture is suitable for the task of recognizing binary images encoded using in-phase and anti-phase oscillations relative to the global clock signal. The phase locking effect makes it possible to achieve cluster synchronization of neurons (both at the input and at the output layer). In this work, a context-dependent algorithm for initiating oscillations of spiking interneurons, which are in an excitable mode, is implemented. As a result, only a fraction of the Hebb connections are employed for the pattern retrieval from memory. The biologically relevant Hodgkin-Huxley-Mainen model is utilized as neurons.

articleTitle: Synchronized UAV Group Flight Control under Data Rate Limitations and Actuator Saturation
publicationTitle: 2023 7th Scientific School Dynamics of Complex Networks and their Applications (DCNA)
abstract: This work specifically addresses the challenges associated with information transfer between agents in pursuit of desired control objectives. Seamless communication is crucial, especially during formation synchronization, as delays can lead to disintegration. Additionally, large-scale systems may face string or mesh instability, where state deviations increase. This work aims to advance decentralized control in multi-agent systems with complex information graph structures, considering nonlinear limitations on the control signal. A sequential nonlinear corrective unit is employed to mitigate this effect. The present study incorporates data rate limitations on information exchange between UAVs in formation. An adaptive coding/decoding procedure is utilized for data transfer, and the minimal data transmission rate required for maintaining formation stability is numerically evaluated.
